verdict.rationale: Granola's own docs describe speaker tags that show each participant's name above their parts of the conversation. That goes beyond the default 'Me and Them' labels and covers the core of named-speaker attribution. The evidence is a single doc line. It does not explain how names are matched, how accurate diarization is, or whether tags are on by default or work in every context. Missing for 10: documented name-matching mechanism (e.g. calendar attendees), diarization accuracy, availability across desktop/mobile/in-person, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, the transcript attributes words to the right named speakers (diarization plus real name matching), not just "Speaker 1/2"

citations.quote: Speaker tags show each participant's name above their parts of the conversation, giving you more detailed attribution than the default Me and Them labels.
